heading: EXT. DRY CREEK BED, SOUTH TEXAS - NOON

units.text: EXT. DRY CREEK BED, SOUTH TEXAS - NOON
White glare on pale stones.
Mesquite and a dead cottonwood.
The creek bed is a crooked ribbon of dust, ankle-deep with the memory of water.
Heat shimmers on the rocks.
Four people stand at the four corners of a small open grave.
A tall MAN in a black frock coat, hat in hand, reads from a Bible.
A shorter WOMAN beside him, in a widow's veil, holds a tiny wooden cross.
An older RANCHER in dusty chaps leans on a shovel.
A BOY of fifteen, barefoot, stares at the hole.
He closes the book.
She steps forward and plants the cross at the head of the grave.
He puts on his hat.
The rancher rests the shovel against his hip and starts to fill the hole, and the boy, after a long moment, takes the spade from him and finishes it himself, tamping each shovelful.
She watches him.
He watches the ground.
The man in black shifts his weight and turns to the rancher.
The rancher spits.
They stand in the heat.
Nobody says a word.
Then the woman lifts her veil.
She is younger than the veil suggested.
She looks at the rancher, then at the man in black, then at the boy.
Who's going to tell him?
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: The three men look at one another.
